identity.description: L2-penalized least squares: shrinks all coefficients toward zero without zeroing any, trading a little bias for a large variance reduction. THE collinearity fixer — the penalty makes X'X + alpha*I invertible, so the solution stays unique and stable where OLS becomes ill-posed (including p > n).

axes.note: closed-form under the default solvers; only sag/saga are stochastic

emits.note: POINT ESTIMATES ONLY — sklearn computes no SEs, and shrunk coefficients are biased estimators anyway; for inference-grade coefficients use ols

alpha.note: the single knob that matters; the useful range spans decades, hence log prior

solver.note: auto picks by data shape; svd is the numerically safest for ill-conditioned X

positive.note: domain-knowledge constraint (forces lbfgs), not a search dimension

invariances.why: the L2 penalty sums squared coefficients across features in their raw units — an unscaled feature's shrinkage depends on its units, so standardization is what makes 'equal penalty' mean equal
linear in the inputs; any monotone transform of a feature changes the least-squares fit
the linear-algebra solvers have no missing-value path; NaN raises
requires a pre-encoded numeric design matrix
squared-error loss presumes a linear mean and is the Gaussian MLE — heavy-tailed noise or y-outliers pull the fit quadratically hard
the penalized normal equations are solvable for ANY n, including p > n where OLS is undefined — ridge is the small-n/wide-data workhorse
the linear predictor extends unboundedly beyond the training range

featureStats.why: ridge exists to fix what VIF measures — the alpha*I term caps the variance inflation of collinear directions, trading bias for a unique, stable solution
kappa(X) quantifies how close X'X is to singular; large kappa is the direct commit-ridge-over-OLS signal because the penalty bounds the smallest eigenvalue away from zero
p approaching or exceeding n is exactly where least squares becomes ill-posed while ridge remains defined
squared loss weights residuals quadratically — a few extreme y values can dominate the objective regardless of the penalty

modelMetrics.why: coefficients that swing wildly across the alpha path expose the collinear directions the penalty is suppressing — stable paths mean the effect story can be trusted
if boosted trees decisively beat ridge, the linearity assumption is leaving signal on the table — a facet toward non-linear families; a tie is a commit-linear signal

edgeCases.behavior: the penalty splits the weight exactly evenly across copies — deterministic, but each per-feature coefficient is halved
degenerates toward the ill-posed OLS solve; solution numerically unstable
quadratic loss lets single rows dominate the fit
edgeCases.note: robust/quantile loss is the family exit

edgeCases.behavior: coefficient driven to ~0 by the penalty; harmless but flags a dead column

canBeSeeds.note: the standard regression stacker — convex and shrinkage-protected against overweighting one base model

placementClaims.why: no native NaN path — the solver raises on missing values
linearizing skewed covariates (log/Yeo-Johnson) improves the linear-mean fit and tames leverage points
the L2 penalty is unit-dependent — the textbook rule: standardize before ridge or the shrinkage is arbitrary across features
categoricals must be design-encoded before the linear-algebra solve
